verified.note: SARS's own PAYE Employer Reconciliation BRS, marked for public release, and the only SARS publication that prints a check algorithm. §8.1 “Modulus 10 check on Income Tax Number” gives the rule and two worked examples for the ten-digit income tax reference number. READ THE SCOPE CAREFULLY: this document covers the income tax number and, separately at §8.2, PAYE/SDL/UIF references — where “the first digit must be replaced with a 4”. It says nothing whatever about VAT registration numbers, so it must not be cited as evidence for one.

note.en: Structure is checked. This record used to say SARS applies a modulus 10 to the VAT number; the cited BRS shows where that belief comes from and does not support it — §8.2's “the first digit must be replaced with a 4” is the PAYE/SDL/UIF rule, not a VAT one, and the leading 4 this format requires is a coincidence of shape. SARS publishes no check rule for VAT registration numbers anywhere this build could find, so the engine stays unimplemented rather than borrowing one that was written for a different number. Confirm against your VAT 103 notice.

Structure only, and that is now a gap rather than a limit. This record used to say SARS publishes no check-digit rule for the income tax reference number — it does: §8.1 of the cited BRS, “Modulus 10 check on Income Tax Number”, gives a Luhn over the first nine digits with two worked examples (0001339050 and 0667056642). Implementing it needs an engine and fixtures, so it is written down here rather than half-done, and the badge still says format only because that is what runs.
No e-invoicing mandate. A VAT number is needed on a tax invoice above the threshold.
